story: Backbone State Park is Iowa's oldest state park, dedicated in 1920 in the USA. It measures 2,001 acres and is heavily forested, mainly in species of oak and maple, featuring a steep ridge of bedrock carved by the Maquoketa River.
matters: The park is part of the Driftless Area, remaining unglaciated during the last Ice Age with ancient dolomite formations and active springs, caves, sinkholes, and karsts.
name: Backbone State Park
